source_title: Treaty with the Six Nations, 1784 (Statutes at Large)
source_quote: Six hostages shall be immediately delivered to the commissioners by
corrected_summary: Article I of the 1784 Fort Stanwix treaty made peace conditional on the Senecas, Mohawks, Onondagas and Cayugas delivering six hostages, to be held until all prisoners were returned; the Art. III boundary followed in the same instrument. The treaty text does not itself show the hostages were already in custody at signing, and the later Six Nations repudiation of the delegates comes from secondary accounts (atlas V003), not from this text.
notes: Hostage clause confirmed verbatim in 7 Stat. 15 and Kappler II. "Signed while those hostages were in US custody" is an inference from "immediately delivered"; needs a primary account (e.g., Olden Time / Craig, or the commissioners journal) before stating it as fact. Royce areas 1 and 2 are the Six Nations cession W. of the line (atlas crosswalk TLA-T-009).

Article VI had the signers acknowledge that lands east, south and west of a reserved Wyandot-Delaware tract (between the Cuyahoga and the Great Miami) belonged to the US.
